audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) All deciding quotations are verbatim in copies we hold (Kießling 2003 author PDF full text; Mous 2022 OA full text; Kießling 2024 as two Google Books snippets). (2) The 'tonal / tonal-accent, no established stress rule' coding rests on specialist but non-primary works: a 2003 comparative tonogenesis article whose Alagwa stress remark is an endnote extrapolated from Burunge, a 2024 handbook chapter seen only in snippet, and Mous 2022 citing his own grammar. The primary description, Mous 2016 (354 pp. reference grammar), is not yet obtained. (3) Evidence gathered now that the grammar will not overturn the classification: both published reviews of Mous 2016 (Harvey 2018 JALL; Kießling 2017 Ethnorêma, downloaded from the publisher's site) itemise the phonology chapter as phonemes, tone (pp. 21-26), intonation (26-29), syllables, restrictions, reduplication, vowel processes, with no stress section, and Kießling

sources.quote: 'The phonological section includes diligent treatments of ... diphthongs (p.30-2), positional and sequential restrictions of vowels (p.32-35) and suprasegmentals other than tone, e.g. an accurate description of intonational patterns (p.26-29) in strict delimitation from tone (p.21-26).' No mention of stress anywhere in the review.

Our record quotes it only second-hand (Mous 2022 citing p. 21) and the third reader flagged 'if Mous 2016 pp. 11-21 states a stress-placement rule, revisit'. Reading pp. 19-29 would settle whether any word-stress statement exists and replace the search-snippet evidence 2024 sentence.
